Here’s a concise overview of the National University of Río Cuarto (Universidad Nacional de Río Cuarto, UNRC) in Argentina.

Basic profile
- Type: Public, national university
- Location: City of Río Cuarto, Córdoba Province, Argentina (main campus on the outskirts of the city)
- Founded: 1971 (part of Argentina’s Plan Taquini expansion of public universities in the late 1960s–70s)
- Language of instruction: Spanish
- Website: https://www.unrc.edu.ar

Academic structure
- Typical faculties (names can vary slightly in translation):
  - Agronomy and Veterinary Sciences
  - Engineering
  - Economic Sciences
  - Human Sciences
  - Exact/Physical/Chemical and Natural Sciences
- Programs: Undergraduate (licenciaturas, engineering degrees, teacher-training/profesorados, veterinary medicine), graduate (specializations, master’s, PhDs).
- Strengths and focus areas:
  - Agriculture, agri-food systems, veterinary medicine, environmental/biological sciences
  - Engineering and applied sciences tied to regional industry
  - Economics, education, social sciences, and humanities

Research and extension
- Active research agenda aligned with regional needs of southern Córdoba and the central Pampas (agronomy, animal health, biotechnology, environmental management, renewable resources).
- Collaborative projects with national research bodies (e.g., CONICET) and public agencies; technology transfer to local producers and SMEs.
- University extension and community engagement are central (farmer outreach, rural development, health and education initiatives).

Campus and facilities
- Large integrated campus with teaching buildings, laboratories, libraries, experimental fields and farms for agronomy and animal science, and facilities supporting engineering and natural sciences.
- Services typically include a university library system, cultural and sports programs; veterinary clinical facilities are commonly available through the Agronomy/Veterinary faculty.

Student body and governance
- Enrollment: commonly cited in the tens of thousands (roughly around 20,000) across undergraduate and graduate levels.
- Governance: co-governed model standard in Argentine national universities (representation of faculty, students, and graduates); led by a rector and a university council; each faculty has its own dean and council.
- Tuition: As with Argentina’s national universities, undergraduate programs have no tuition fees for domestic students; most entrants complete a leveling/introductory course rather than a competitive entrance exam. Some graduate programs may charge fees.

Internationalization
- Exchange agreements and mobility programs with Latin American and European universities; participation in Argentine and regional networks.
- Support offices for international students and research collaboration.

Regional role
- UNRC plays a key role in the socio-economic development of southern Córdoba, especially in agri-food value chains (grains, oilseeds, dairy, livestock), environmental stewardship, education, and public policy support.

If you want specifics—current degree lists, research institutes, admissions timelines, or exact faculty names—I can pull them from the university site or recent catalogs.
